extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities (contractors/grantees), child welfare providers, legal service providers, and public commenters/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed ORR regulations setting definitions, minimum standards, contingency planning, placement criteria, review processes, and hearing procedures for care and placement of unaccompanied children (including emergency/influx facilities and restrictive placements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Influx (85% threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Influx means a situation in which the net bed capacity of ORR's existing capacity in standard programs that is occupied or held for placement by unaccompanied children meets or exceeds 85 percent for a period of seven consecutive days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR departs from the FSA numeric threshold approach and uses capacity-based measure to reflect significant increases that exceed federal processing, transport, or sheltering capabilities; placements at emergency/influx facilities cease when capacity drops below 85% for seven consecutive days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Emergency or Influx Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or Influx Facilities: a single term to encompass a care provider facility opened in response to either an emergency or influx; may be contracted for and stood up in advance but no children are placed until an emergency or influx exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facilities are intended as temporary responses and may be activated in advance but only used when an emergency/influx is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and regular reevaluation (§410.1800(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would regularly reevaluate the number of placements needed to determine whether shelters, heightened supervision facilities, and transitional home care beds should be adjusted to accommodate changes in unaccompanied children eligible for placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular reevaluation supports ORR's preference to place children in licensed standard programs and helps expedite placement into licensed programs during influx/emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable efforts to place in standard programs (§410.1800(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of an emergency or influx preventing prompt placement in standard programs, ORR shall make all reasonable efforts to place each unaccompanied child in a standard program as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with paragraph 12A of the FSA; ORR's ongoing reevaluation of placements should facilitate rapid placement in licensed programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency activities during influx (§410.1800(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: During an influx ORR implements its contingency plan (which may include opening facilities), continually develops standard programs available to accept placements, and maintains a list of affected unaccompanied children with specified identifying and placement data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required list must include each child's name; date and country of birth; date of placement in ORR custody; and place and date of current placement to support tracking and case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility licensure and compliance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities may not be licensed or may be exempted from licensing, but regardless of licensure status they must meet ORR standards and comply to the greatest extent possible with state child welfare laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR preference is licensed facilities when possible; ORR will review conflicts between ORR regulations and state law to ensure statutory responsibilities are met; federal duties of ORR employees prevail where conflict exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum physical care and maintenance (§410.1801(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must provide unaccompanied children with proper physical care and maintenance, including suitable living accommodations, food, appropriate clothing, and personal grooming items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the baseline material/housing needs required to open and operate a facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical and dental services (§410.1801(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide appropriate routine medical and dental care; family planning services including pregnancy tests; emergency healthcare services; a complete medical exam (including infectious disease screenings) generally within 48 hours of admission; immunizations as recommended by ACIP; administration of prescribed medication and special diets; and appropriate mental health interventions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health services must meet ORR timelines (e.g., 48-hour exam) and accepted public health immunization guidance; some services may require heightened ORR involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized needs assessment (§410.1801(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unaccompanied child must receive an individualized needs assessment including initial intake forms, essential identification and family history, identification of special needs requiring immediate intervention, educational assessment and plan, assessment of family relationships and interactions, statement of religious preference, assessment of personal goals/strengths/weaknesses, and identifying information for potential relatives or others who could assist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should capture immediate health and safety needs and longer-term social, educational, and family connection information to inform care planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational services requirement (§410.1801(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency or influx facilities must provide educational services appropriate to the child's development and communication skills in a structured classroom setting Monday through Friday, concentrating on basic academic competencies and secondarily on English Language Training; provide instruction and materials in needed languages; and cover basic subjects (Science, Social Studies, Math, Reading, Writing, PE) plus reading materials in languages other than English for leisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to avoid learning loss; programs must be language-appropriate and structured while prioritizing basic competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recreation and leisure time plan (§410.1801(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide activities per a recreation/leisure plan including daily outdoor activity (weather permitting) with at least one hour/day of large muscle activity and one hour/day of structured leisure activities (not TV); when school is not in session, activities should increase to a total of three hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recreation requirements support physical and psychosocial wellbeing; structured leisure should be active and not passive screen time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual counseling frequency (§410.1801(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide at least one individual counseling session per week conducted by trained social work staff to review progress, set short-term objectives, and address developmental and crisis-related needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counseling must be by trained staff with specific objectives tied to the child's care plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group counseling frequency and purpose (§410.1801(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide group counseling sessions at least twice a week, typically informal, with all children present to allow acclimation to staff, peers, and program rules and to discuss daily program management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group sessions offer forum for expression, problem resolution, and orientation to program expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acculturation and adaptation services (§410.1801(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide acculturation and adaptation services, including information on developing social and interpersonal skills necessary for independent and responsible living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services are intended to support social development and cultural needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive orientation (§410.1801(b)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide a comprehensive orientation regarding program intent, services, rules (written and verbal), expectations, and the availability of legal assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orientation should clearly explain program operations and legal rights/options to children upon arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to religious services and conscience protections (§410.1801(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide access to religious services of the child's choice whenever possible and operate in compliance with RFRA, applicable federal conscience protections, other federal civil rights laws, and HHS regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for spiritual practices must be balanced with applicable federal requirements and nondiscrimination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visitation and family contact (§410.1801(b)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must make visitation and contact with family members available (regardless of immigration status) in a structured way to encourage visitation while staff respect the child's privacy and prevent unauthorized release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visitation policies should facilitate family connection but include safeguards for child safety and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to privacy protections (§410.1801(b)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Children have a reasonable right to privacy, including wearing their own clothes when available; private space for personal belongings; private phone conversations and visits as permitted by house rules; and sending/receiving uncensored mail unless there's a reasonable belief it contains contraband.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy protections must be balanced with safety considerations and house rules; limitations only where reasonable belief of contraband exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative identification and guardianship assistance (§410.1801(b)(13))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide services designed to identify relatives in the U.S. and foreign countries and assist in obtaining legal guardianship when necessary for release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports family reunification and lawful release pathways when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal services information and access (§410.1801(b)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must provide unaccompanied children with legal services information including availability of free legal assistance, the right to a removal hearing before an immigration judge, ability to apply for asylum with USCIS, and ability to request voluntary departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information must be accessible and help children understand their legal options; notably representation may be at no expense to the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with state codes and mandatory reporting (§410.1801(b)(15))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether state-licensed or not, facilities must comply to the greatest extent possible with state child welfare laws (e.g., mandatory reporting) and applicable state/local building, fire, health and safety codes; ORR will review conflicts to meet statutory responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where state requirements conflict with federal duties of ORR employees, Federal duties control; ORR will assess conflicts case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and language sensitivity; individual service plan (§410.1801(b)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must deliver services sensitive to the age, culture, native language, and needs of each child and develop an individual service plan for each child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual service plans operationalize culturally and developmentally appropriate care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records, reporting, and confidentiality (§410.1801(b)(17))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must maintain case files, make regular reports to ORR, and have accountability systems that preserve confidentiality and protect records from unauthorized use or disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and reporting enable oversight; confidentiality protections are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/sanitary and safety conditions (§410.1801(c)(1)-(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must: maintain safe and sanitary conditions; provide access to toilets/showers/sinks and hygiene items; provide drinking water and food; provide emergency medical assistance; maintain adequate temperature control/ventilation; provide adequate supervision; separate children with past criminal/juvenile detention histories or perpetrated sexual abuse that present danger; provide contact with family members arrested with the child; and provide access to legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are based partly on FSA paragraph 12A and apply additional safeguards for minors; intended to protect physical safety, health, and legal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language access requirements (subpart D and §410.1306 linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must consistently offer interpretation services in a child's native or preferred language to the greatest extent practicable for intake, orientation, healthcare, sexual assault/abuse program information, and legal services; ORR may transfer a child to provide adequate language services; case managers must have on-site presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language access is critical to ensure children understand rights/options and obtain effective legal representation; facilities should proactively offer interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers for emergency/influx facilities (§410.1801(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may grant waivers from one or all services in §410.1801(b) if the facility is activated for six consecutive months or less and ORR determines the standards are operationally infeasible; determinations are case-by-case and waivers must be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are limited-duration, based on operational infeasibility during short-term activations, and publicly disclosed for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement eligibility criteria for emergency/influx facilities (§410.1802(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible, children placed in emergency/influx facilities should: be expected to be released to a sponsor within 30 days; be age 13 or older; speak English or Spanish as preferred language; not have known disability/mental health/medical/dental issues requiring additional evaluation or monitoring; not be pregnant or parenting teens; not have diminution of legal services due to transfer; and not be a danger to self or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a child is later found not to meet criteria, ORR will transfer the child to the least restrictive appropriate setting as expeditiously as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional placement factors to consider (§410.1802(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR should consider factors such as: not placing children who are in sibling groups with siblings ≤12; not placing children with pending age determinations; not placing children involved in active investigations (licensing, CPS, law enforcement, sexual abuse); not placing children with pending home studies; not placing children turning 18 within 30 days; not placing children scheduled for discharge in three days or less; not placing children with current immigration or family court docket dates or pending adjustment or with an attorney of record; ensuring medical clearance and vaccinations; and avoiding placing children with known mental health/dental/medical issues including contagious diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors support safe and appropriate placements and help avoid administrative/legal/service access disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of administrative review for restrictive placements (Subpart J purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subpart's purpose is to describe the availability of review of certain ORR decisions regarding the care and placement of unaccompanied children, especially restrictive placements, to ensure least restrictive settings consistent with safety and best interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review is fundamental to ensure restrictive placements are appropriate and based on clear and convincing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for restrictive placements and evidentiary requirement (§410.1901)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must place children in the least restrictive setting in their best interests, considering danger to self, danger to the community, and runaway risk; for restrictive placements ORR must determine based on clear and convincing evidence that sufficient grounds exist to step up or continue holding the child in a restrictive placement, and record the supporting evidence in the child's case file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This elevates the evidentiary threshold for restrictive placements and requires documentation in case files for review and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Placement (NOP) timing and content (§410.1901(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A written NOP must be provided to the child no later than 48 hours after a step-up to restrictive placement and at least every 30 days while the child remains in restrictive placement. The NOP must clearly set forth the reason(s) for placement and a summary of supporting evidence; inform the child of their right to contest the placement before the Placement Review Panel and other administrative review procedures; include explanation of the right to be represented by counsel; and a case manager must explain the NOP to the child in the child's native/preferred language in a way the child understands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications are intended to ensure children understand reasons for restrictive placement and available remedies; communications must meet language access standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of NOP to counsel/advocates/parents (§410.1901(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must provide a copy of the NOP to the child's legal counsel of record, legal service provider, child advocate, and a parent or legal guardian of record no later than 48 hours after step-up and every 30 days thereafter, subject to child welfare-related exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures relevant parties and representatives are informed to enable timely challenges and advocacy, with privacy-related exceptions as warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review intervals for restrictive placements (§410.1901(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular administrative reviews are required at 30-day minimum intervals for all restrictive placements; more intensive 45-day reviews by ORR supervisory staff are required for secure facilities; for RTCs the 30-day review must involve a psychiatrist or psychologist to assess continued need for restrictive residential care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent reviews aim to limit duration of restrictive placements and involve clinical expertise where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement Review Panel (PRP) procedures and rights (§410.1902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Children may request reconsideration of restrictive placement and ORR convenes a PRP (typically a three-member panel of senior-level career staff with child welfare experience) to review requests; children may have counsel assistance, present evidence, call witnesses, cross-examine ORR witnesses (if willing), and receive their case file information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRP hearings provide an administrative forum for contesting restrictive placements with rights to be heard and access to evidence; children may also submit written reconsideration with supporting documents instead of a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRP timing, decision deadlines, and recusal (§410.1902(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must convene the PRP within a reasonable timeframe; the PRP should issue a decision within 30 calendar days of request whenever possible; ORR staff involved in the decision to step-up a child may not serve on the PRP for that child's review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness and impartiality requirements ensure prompt and unbiased reconsideration of restrictive placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk determination hearings before independent HHS hearing officer (§410.1903)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would afford all children in restrictive placements a risk determination hearing before an independent HHS hearing officer to determine by written decision whether the child would present a danger to the community if released, unless the child refuses in writing; other children in custody may also request such hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hearings parallel bond-type reviews but within HHS and focus on dangerousness (runaway risk is not considered). They are intended to be independent and timely and may be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and burdens for risk determination hearings (§410.1903(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR bears an initial burden of production to provide relevant arguments and documents supporting dangerousness; the unaccompanied child bears the burden of persuasion to show non-danger by a preponderance of the evidence; children may be represented by chosen persons, present oral/written evidence, appear by video/teleconference; ORR may present evidence in writing or by appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR has duties to make documents available timely; the hearing process provides procedural rights similar to immigration bond hearings but adapted to the ORR/HHS context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding effect and appealability of hearing decisions (§410.1903(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision that a child would not be a danger to the community if released is binding on ORR unless appealed; ORR believes children must have availability to appeal decisions finding they are a danger to the community if released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions favorable to release are immediately binding absent appeal; adverse findings are subject to appeal to ensure further review.
